The SDK-owned tracked handle reuses concrete UpdateOpts and With options; current-value assignment equality gives clean same-value/no-change commits, sticky A-to-B-to-A dirty fields, and null tombstones when a cached mutable field is removed. Only dirty fields reach the PATCH200 object envelope; profile metadata preserves omission, null and empty-object presence.

Track owns an authoritative cached Body or a typed-only local seed without invented HTTP evidence; Value and Response are deep snapshots of the merged cache and last successful response fields. Explicit Load IDs remain fixed and exact Name lookup occurs once even when response IDs change, are null or are omitted.

Valid responses shallow-merge whole fields, replace nested objects, preserve omitted cached values and clean accepted revisions even when an edited field is omitted. Refresh GETs the fixed ID and resets pre-fetch revisions; edits made during Commit or Refresh survive response merge and remain dirty for the next explicit commit.

Invalid edits and body/query/auth-header commit options fail atomically before HTTP, including clean commits; canceled contexts and invalid selected service/version remain errors. Native HTTP and transport failures preserve their cause and dirty state. Accepted malformed responses retain raw HTTP evidence in ResponseError, keep the last valid response and never trigger an automatic mutation resend.

differences: Stateless Update sends explicit fields and rejects an empty request; cached lifecycle is the separate concrete Track/Load plus Edit/Commit/Refresh API, with snapshots instead of mutating or returning the original Python Resource pointer. The official mutable core is name and metadata. Go rejects known readonly fields and case-variant typed collisions; explicit RemoveName and profile RemoveMetadata send null tombstones, whose server acceptance is not assumed. Python permissive descriptors/attrs and implicit Body coercion are replaced by concrete owned options; explicit unknown vendor fields are a documented Go extension.

Track uses raw cached Body and its decoded ID when present, ignoring caller mutations to exported typed fields; typed-only models are local seeds rather than evidence of an HTTP response. Explicit Load preserves the request ID, exact Name lookup uses one list resolution, and response IDs never retarget subsequent requests.

JSON numbers compare exactly and booleans remain distinct from numbers, unlike Python True-equals-1 assignment comparison. Unknown response fields are preserved, Value.Body is the merged cache, and Response.Body contains last successful response fields; a manual Track Response remains the local seed until HTTP succeeds.

Clean Commit validates context, selected service/version and options and returns without HTTP even with valid header-only options. Header dirtiness and allow_empty_commit do not force an empty Go PATCH; newer concurrent edits are revision-protected rather than cleared by an older response.

The documented object envelope and success200 are strict. Python flat/empty fallback and ignored non-parseable responses are replaced by ResponseError with accepted HTTP evidence; failure keeps dirty state and the SDK does not automatically retry, so callers can Refresh before an explicit resend.

Endpoint, authentication and numeric microversion belong to the selected client. contracts.behavior: WaitForServer supplies ACTIVE, exact case-insensitive ERROR, two-second polling and120-second SDK timeout. WaitForServerState keeps the same server-specific timeout with an explicit target; it is distinct from unlimited generic Compute WaitForState. The returned model is the actual native observation, not a cached supplied Python Resource.

Target state comparison precedes failure comparison. WithFailureStates replaces the exact case-insensitive default list, and an empty list disables state failure checks. error_deleting/error_extending, failed or killed are not inferred as additional service failures. Captured failure-state values remain independent of later caller slice mutations.

SDK defaults are prepended and concrete caller resource.WaitOption values apply last. WithUnlimitedWait removes a finite default, a later positive WithTimeout reinstates a bound, and parent context deadlines and cancellation remain effective. No application status adapter or polling builder is required.

The default polling interval is two seconds and a positive caller interval replaces it. Nil context or collection, invalid refs/targets/options, unsupported selected attributes and canceled context fail without HTTP. Callback cancellation and active-fetch cancellation stop before any further poll.

Status selection uses an exported string field and can also select deletion completion. Server canonical integer progress reports native values; absent canonical progress reports zero. Cinder-v3 Snapshot uses the noncanonical os-extended-snapshot-attributes:progress string tag, so callback reports zero without parsing that string. Successful terminal, failure and HTTP-error observations do not invoke the callback.

Explicit ID is stable even when response ID differs. Existing Name lookup resolves once, retains the native list/name-query boundary, and state waiting reports its initial List observation before fixed-ID GETs. Selected ResourceBase/reverse prefix, configured ordinary headers/microversion, caller context/middleware and the original live Provider token remain in use; no response-driven route or model synthesis occurs.

Fresh lookup failures remain errors rather than a successful target model. The shared read gate preserves original terminal URL/accepted-response/JSON/read/context causes even when nested native404 or adapter-owned ErrNotFound is discoverable. Actual direct403 or transport-wrapped404 terminates the service deletion observation after one request. Successful missing state fetches return a nonpanic error; successful nil deletion fetches complete.

Existing common Collection.Wait/WaitDeleted and generated WaitFor/WaitForDeletion retain their five-minute deadline and original binding failure predicate. Native WaitForStatus retains its error-only callable and native predicate-first behavior, including original caller context; source one-second/exact-case behavior is not replaced by this service policy. This is preservation evidence, not a separate native-operation status promotion.

Generator discovery records only the six audited Server/Cinder Volume-Snapshot/Image-v2 collections with their service wait policy. Existing generated common WaitFor/WaitForDeletion still delegate unchanged; unrelated Backup, Flavor, Task, network and Image-v1 collections receive no inferred service-default policy.

differences: Go accepts explicit resource.Ref and an SDK typed collection and returns a native-model pointer for state waits; Python accepts an existing Resource and may return it immediately from its cached target state without HTTP. A selected396 response with missing input or missing/null/empty type fails before POST, retaining the actual fetched result; no seeded/cached request data is invented.

Each successful creation changes the fixed current ID only after a usable canonical lowercase POST id is validated. Repeated396 transitions keep one unchanged deadline across GET/POST/new-GET rather than starting new120-second budgets. The waiter pauses and fetches the new ID even if the actual POST201 model already reports success. A deadline during that pause returns the actual created model and201 proof with the context error, without a success shortcut or another GET. The outer Task/Body/Header/StatusCode retain the latest successfully decoded real observation. Created separately retains the latest accepted POST201 body/header/status, including read/decode/ID failures with no invented Task. Failed recreation keeps the previous fetched model/route; failed subsequent GET keeps the valid created model/current ID. Request headers are canonicalized, frozen and applied across the workflow; case-insensitive sequential helpers are last-wins. Nil context/source/provider/options, unsafe or Name refs, blank targets/failures and nonpositive helper durations also reject without HTTP. The task namespace provides no generic progress/status-attribute/query/base-path controls.

Existing native Get/Create/List declarations, Task alias and generic collection wait boundary remain separate. Generator metadata marks only the audited image-v2 Task collection with task_wait=WaitForTask; parent/payload drift and unrelated resource inference are rejected, without emitting the manual workflow as a native declaration.

The shared workflow timeout applies to active requests as well as pauses and remains subordinate to parent context; timeout/cancellation exposes Go context causes rather than Python ResourceTimeout. Positive duration helpers and explicit Unlimited replace Python interval-zero normalization and zero/negative wait behavior.

TaskWaitResult distinguishes the latest successful observation from the latest accepted creation proof, preserves partial results/errors and uses separately owned evidence. Python normally returns the current Resource or raises; the Go result does not invent a server task after an unaccepted or undecodable response.

SDK-owned explicit header options snapshot requests and preserve original Provider transport policy. contracts.behavior: ImportImage starts with a fresh metadata GET of the explicit ID. ImportKnownImage copies only supplied native ID/container/disk formats before option callbacks and sends no GET. The default request is one glance-direct POST with no empty URI or seeded model fields; incidental response IDs never retarget the requested import ID.

An explicit Name uses the existing Images collection exact-name and advertised native paging resolver once, then freshly GETs the resolved ID rather than reusing listed formats. Case decoys, missing names, duplicate matches and errors on later pages terminate before metadata GET or import POST.

Fresh metadata must be a flat UTF-8 object accepted as200, decode the complete native Image shape, and contain canonical lowercase nonempty container_format/disk_format strings. Missing/null/case-only/typed-invalid formats or unrelated malformed native fields/time preserve actual accepted GET body/header/status with ResponseError and never POST.

Owned method options default empty Method to glance-direct and preserve unknown nonempty server methods. Web URI is required and prohibited for other methods. Glance-download requires region+image ID and emits optional interface only when present; incomplete/orphan/wrong-method remote values reject before lookup.

Singular Store selects only X-Image-Meta-Store while plural Stores selects only the root JSON array. Explicit false root booleans remain present; nil booleans and nil/empty Stores omit. Store plus nonempty Stores or true AllStores conflicts, and explicit empty Store/empty entries reject; an inherited legacy store header conflicts with plural/all-store selection before HTTP.

Root Fields and MethodFields are separate SDK-owned JSON extension namespaces. Snapshot encoding retains nested JSON, null and exact json.Number values; protected core keys and aliases cannot replace method/store/booleans or method name/URI/remote controls. Non-JSON values fail before HTTP.

Ordinary headers are canonicalized with sequential last-wins helpers, frozen and independently reused. Different values under case aliases and protected auth/transport/version/store headers reject. A configured explicit image version header must agree with the selected source Microversion.

WithImportOpts snapshots pointers, Stores slices, header maps and both nested JSON extension maps and replaces the whole options value; individual helpers apply afterward. Bulk empty restores the default method and clears prior controls. Parsed custom configs, supplied KnownImage mutation during options and concurrent reusable options do not alter frozen request data or another response.

ImportResult reports the fixed ImageID and only actual accepted202 Body/Header/StatusCode. Empty, arbitrary acknowledgement and large-number bytes are passive owned evidence, not an active Image/Task model. A foreign Location is retained without following it or deriving identity.

Native HTTP/transport, context and accepted body-read failures stay terminal submission errors without fabricated acknowledgements or semantic resend/cleanup. Accepted202 read failure returns the actual partial result and ResponseError; a concurrently expired context is joined with the original native404 evidence instead of hiding either cause.

The workflow captures client settings/headers and fixes ResourceBase-aware metadata GET/import POST routes while sharing the original Provider. Live token rotation, request context, selected Microversion and configured middleware survive GET/POST; configured401 reauth and503 retry retain the same import body and target. Invalidating source changes after options or GET stop before the next phase, redirects cannot change the image, and explicit Store overlays the configured legacy value without modifying the original client.

Size is an optional nonnegative int64 pointer: nil omits and zero is preserved in X-OpenStack-Image-Size only. No Content-Length or whole-file length is inferred, and no caller data is truncated to the stated size.

Binary PUT uses a private fixed-target Provider with reauthentication, retry, backoff and redirects disabled, preserving the original client settings. Partial consumption followed by native status, transport or reader failure is not semantically replayed or followed by metadata GET.

WithStageOpts snapshots Size and header maps and replaces the complete config; individual helpers apply afterward. Parsed custom options and reusable concurrent options remain independent; each caller retains ownership of its reader.

Before any accepted PUT204 the result is nil. Accepted PUT read or followup GET failures return the actual acknowledgement plus original errors without synthetic uploading/active models, extra recovery GET, import POST or cleanup DELETE. Context causes remain inspectable alongside original failures.

Source client/provider/type/header/origin validity is checked before options and subsequent phases. Captured ServiceClient routes, Microversion and header maps remain fixed; the original Provider token is read at dispatch. Each metadata GET keeps the configured JSON retry/auth policy and selected HTTPClient transport/timeout, while binary PUT disables replay callbacks on its private provider.

Existing native Stage/Upload/Download functions, StageResult alias and specialized inventory placeholder remain separate. Actual compiled signature and canonical Image ID/status tag guards reject drift without inventing a resource collection or changing generated native declarations.

Python filename and existing Resource.data inputs are separate from explicit borrowed io.Reader. Python infers seekable whole-file size, restoring its cursor, and accepts bool or negative int; Go omits automatic size and accepts only optional nonnegative int64, preserving zero and current-position streaming.

The Go binary provider disables SDK reauthentication, retry, backoff and redirects to prevent reader replay. Caller RoundTripper internals and release of a blocking Read remain outside the one-SDK-PUT guarantee; the underlying reader is never closed or sought.

Go keeps actual accepted PUT204 Acknowledgement evidence separate from the final GET model/response, and can return partial evidence with an error. Python mutates and fetches the same Resource and returns it, without this owned partial-result structure.

Go fresh metadata uses strict accepted200, full native Image decoding, UTF-8 and canonical queued status; native extension map/number/timestamp projection remains native. remaining: Full mutable Image Resource defaults/descriptors/coercion/dirty state, alternate identity, response/header merge and cache semantics are not reproduced by concrete native model/ref APIs.
Python filename opening, existing Resource.data, whole-file automatic size and arbitrary session/adapter injection remain outside this explicit reader workflow.

Proxy fetch cache/skip-cache, configured source response/error policy and general Resource continuation/transport behavior are not fully reconstructed by strict native JSON requests and partial accepted acknowledgements.

Image creation, interoperable import, method discovery, completion waiting, storage cleanup and end-to-end cloud upload composition are separate capabilities. Local HTTP tests do not establish deployment feature/version, quota, permissions, backend capacity or size-validation outcome.
Reader cancellation cannot forcibly release a caller blocking Read without caller cooperation, and custom RoundTripper internal replay is not controlled by the SDK.

contracts.behavior: CreateAndImport defaults to qcow2/bare/private and glance-direct with waiting disabled. Direct execution performs actual creation201, staging204, post-stage metadata200 and import202 without an initial image lookup, duplicate/discovery request or synthetic active result. Phase responses and fixed ImageID are retained separately.

Concrete metadata, stage, import and wait policies, source/reference validity, reader requirements and protected namespaces are checked before the first create POST or input read. Typed nil, invalid source/context, unknown fresh workflow method, conflicting selector and invalid field/header/size/wait policies stop locally.

PrepareStageOptions validates the selected source, applies a caller callback once and returns independently owned concrete size/header settings without HTTP or reader use. Retained callback configuration cannot later alter the prepared snapshot; invalid configured source headers are rejected before callbacks.

PrepareImportOptions is a local-only source-aware snapshot seam. It preserves owned JSON extension numbers and store slices after one callback application, rejects conflicting configured store headers and selected plural/all-store controls, and permits an explicit singular-store overlay without changing the shared source.

The original lowercase creation id must be a nonempty safe route segment and becomes the fixed workflow ImageID. Typed case aliases, foreign Location and later response IDs do not retarget staging, import or wait. Direct creation also requires exact canonical queued status before consuming Data.

Direct import reads required lowercase container_format and disk_format from the actual post-stage metadata body, independently of returned typed case aliases or stale creation formats. Missing/null/empty canonical decision fields preserve the actual accepted response and stop before import.

The workflow metadata policy reuses the existing upload builder, retaining optional false and explicit min_disk/min_ram zero and root JSON extensions without replacing protected core fields. Full and namespace helpers snapshot pointers, slices, maps and JSON. Deferred leaf callback batches run once during preparation and can be cleared by later concrete helpers; reusable policies remain independent. Invalid custom JSON retains the original MarshalerError and caller cause alongside ErrInvalidOption.

Fresh web-download and glance-download workflows create metadata and submit import with no reader or staging phase. Required URI/remote inputs and unused stage controls are guarded before creation. Remote formats come from the actual creation response, plural stores retain repeats and explicit false flags, and singular Store remains header-only. Copy-image and unknown fresh methods are unsupported while the existing leaf passthrough remains separate.

Direct data is borrowed at its current cursor without input Close/Seek/size inspection/buffering or semantic replay. Stage headers and metadata POST-only headers are kept in their selected phases, while size is header-only and explicit zero can be retained. The binary provider replay policy stays distinct from configured JSON requests.

Before accepted creation201 the result is nil; accepted creation read/decode/invariant errors retain Created evidence. Later stage/read/followup/import failures preserve prior actual201/204/200/202 proof and original errors without automatic delete, recreation, recovery GET or fabricated model. Response bodies/headers and models from different phases are independently owned.

Optional active waiting uses concrete SDK-owned policy: nil Wait disables, selected nil timeout/interval use five minutes/two seconds, zero timeout removes the SDK deadline, nil failures select killed/deleted and nonnil empty failures disable them. The parent context bounds all phases; only an actual successful wait populates Ready and prior accepted phase proof remains on failure.

The workflow captures one original-provider client selection and validates its source between phases and waiter polls. Canonical decisions and actual native header/model extraction stay separate from raw evidence; native Create/Get/Stage/Upload and existing Service.Upload remain independently callable without changing generated native declarations or inventory. Generation checks required native CreateOpts/Image field types and canonical JSON tags, rejects drift, and documents the upper workflow independently of native image API declarations.

differences: CreateAndImport is an explicit fresh-image import workflow with qcow2/bare/private, glance-direct and no-wait defaults. Python create_image additionally selects metadata-only/direct-file/configured Swift task paths and uses cloud format/vendor/container configuration.

Go prepares and freezes concrete metadata/stage/import/wait policy before POST or reader consumption, using local-only SDK seams and separate callback namespaces. Python kwargs/meta conversion, descriptor values and mutable Resource/session behavior are broader.

Python non-task _upload_image_put does not receive create_image wait or timeout. Go optional active wait is an explicit five-minute/two-second policy, with caller overrides and parent context, rather than a reproduction of timeout3600 for that source branch.

Go preserves actual accepted201/204/200/202 phase evidence and performs no cleanup DELETE after failure. Python checks response import-method capability after creation, stages without this post-stage metadata GET and deletes upload/import/checksum failures inside its try block.

Go canonical created ID and original lowercase post-stage format decisions reject missing/unsafe data while typed case aliases and passive Location cannot choose the route. Go retains native typed projection/header behavior alongside independent raw response evidence.

Go explicit plural stores and optional false flags are preserved together, while Python stores-is-not-None suppresses both all-store flags. Existing leaf singular Store is header-only rather than Python header plus one-element stores body.

Go borrows explicit io.Reader without filename/name inference, hashing, automatic whole-file size or checksum validation. Binary staging disables SDK replay callbacks and redirects; caller RoundTripper internals and blocking Read release remain caller responsibilities.
remaining: Cloud configuration image_format/vendor flags, automatic Swift object/container and image_api_use_tasks selection, task workflow/cleanup and configuration-specific upload/import capability handling are not reproduced by this explicit workflow.

Python filename opening/name inference, bytes/string/file polymorphism, MD5/SHA256 calculation and duplicate hash freshness shortcut, synthesized owner_specified/legacy shade properties, legacy checksum fetch/compare and seekable whole-file size remain outside the concrete reader API.

Python kwargs integer/string/raw conversion and meta precedence, full mutable Image Resource defaults/descriptors/coercion/dirty state/alternate identity/cache/seed/header merge and injected session/adapter behavior remain unresolved.

Deployment method/storage availability, URL policy, quota, permissions, actual backend processing, eventual import state and end-to-end cloud success are server-owned. Local HTTP proof does not establish those outcomes or a full create_image mapping.

Response models keep native numeric/timestamp/unknown-property projection limits; raw response evidence does not make typed Image precision or arbitrary source Resource semantics exact. Shared wait returns no original response body/header/status or last-failure image evidence.

Custom RoundTripper internal replay and forcibly unblocking a caller reader are outside the SDK one-binary-provider-attempt guarantee. The SDK deliberately avoids cleanup and leaves retained side effects for caller decisions.

contracts.behavior: DownloadTo defaults to metadata GET200 then full binary GET200, using a bounded 1MiB copy chunk and available checksum verification. It retains independent actual native Image, raw metadata body/header/status, actual accepted binary header/status and exact BytesWritten without keeping the full payload or fabricating completion.

Service/source/provider/context/ref/writer and concrete options are validated before any HTTP or Write. Nil and typed-nil writers, invalid route/source/header/Range/If-Range controls, nil callbacks, nonpositive or over64MiB chunks and malformed store preferences stop locally. Nil chunk selects1MiB and nil verification selects true; explicit false remains distinct.

Whole-policy and leaf helpers snapshot pointers and preferences for last replacement, independent reuse and concurrent application. Custom callbacks run once before requests and their retained configuration cannot alter transfer options. Preferences preserve order and duplicates in one URL-encoded comma-separated prefer value; nil/empty omit it.

Explicit ID chooses one fresh metadata GET; Name uses existing exact-name full-page resolution followed by fresh GET. The exact lowercase canonical metadata id must equal the fixed chosen ID. Incidental typed case aliases and response self/file/schema/Location cannot choose the binary route. Actual native projection remains separate from original response evidence; Name pager continuation keeps existing native semantics.

Canonical complete nonempty os_hash_algo/os_hash_value wins over legacy metadata checksum, which wins over literal binary Content-MD5. Incomplete pairs fall back; disabled verification skips canonical hash-field validation while retaining native Image decode. The bounded algorithms md5/sha1/sha224/sha256/sha384/sha512/sha512_224/sha512_256 are implemented. Unsupported primary algorithms and malformed canonical hash types fail before binary GET. Expected strings are not hex-normalized or base64-decoded.

Only actual binary200/204 are accepted. Actual204 performs no Write, clears checksum evidence and retains header/status. Unsolicited206 or HTTP errors retain metadata plus original native rejection without an accepted binary status claim. Metadata-selected algorithm/expected survive binary open/rejection failures. Nonempty Content-Range on actual200 is rejected before Write with accepted200/header and selected metadata proof retained.

Before accepted metadata200 the result is nil. Accepted metadata read/decode/canonical/native-model failures retain raw200 body/header/status and original error, stop before binary GET and do not Write. Later file/open/read/write/short-write failures retain prior metadata, any actual accepted binary response and exact writer-reported successful bytes without rollback, body replay or recovery requests.

The borrowed writer is never closed, sought or truncated. The owned chunk loop does not use ReaderFrom/WriterTo shortcuts, enforces short writes and counts reported written bytes. Simultaneous read/write errors, accepted-body Close errors and context/custom causes remain inspectable. SDK accepted bodies close once and native Request owns rejected bodies. Actual/Complete require full EOF and successful writes; Verified requires a matching digest. Typed DownloadChecksumMismatchError unwraps ErrChecksumMismatch and carries algorithm/expected/actual.
